Question 1: What is your current career stage?

1. Undergraduate student
2. Master's student
3. Ph.D. student
4. Postdoctoral researcher
5. Faculty
6. Non-faculty professional
7. Other (specify)

</div>

<div class = "col-md-6">

```{r q1preplot, message=FALSE}
# Replacing numerical responses with strings
data$pre1a <- gsub(1, "Undergraduate", data$pre1a)
data$pre1a <- gsub(2, "Master's", data$pre1a)
data$pre1a <- gsub(3, "Doctoral", data$pre1a)
data$pre1a <- gsub(4, "Postdoctoral", data$pre1a)
data$pre1a <- gsub(5, "Faculty", data$pre1a)
data$pre1a <- gsub(6, "Professional", data$pre1a)
data$pre1a <- gsub(7, "Other", data$pre1a)

# Categorizing "Other" responses
other <- data$pre1b[which(data$pre1a == "Other")]
data$pre1a[5] <- "Doctoral"
data$pre1a[12] <- "Doctoral"
data$pre1a[28] <- "Doctoral"
data$pre1a[48] <- "Post\nBaccalaureate"

# Plotting output 
levels <- c("Undergraduate", "Post\nBaccalaureate", "Master's", "Doctoral", "Postdoctoral", "Faculty", "Professional")
plot_q1pre <- ggplot(data = subset(data, !is.na(pre1a)), aes(x = factor(pre1a, levels = levels))) +
  geom_bar(fill = color1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ..count..), stat = "count", hjust = 1.25, color = "white", size = 4) +
  scale_x_discrete(drop = F) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size=8,color="black"),
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        panel.border = element_blank())
ggsave("./output/q1pre.png",plot_q1pre,width=6,height=4)
include_graphics("./output/q1pre.png")

# Getting sample size
N <- sum(!is.na(data$pre1a))
cat("N = ", N)
```

Question 2: What were your initial goals when you applied for this workshop? Check all that apply.

1. Learn about the kinds of questions that phylogenetic methods of historical biogeography can answer
2. Learn more about different types of models
3. Learn more about software tools
4. Try out coding a model with the help of workshop facilitators
5. Decide whether to do future research using phylogenetic methods of historical biogeography
6. Discuss research ideas with workshop facilitators and other participants
7. Network with other researchers
8. Add the workshop to a resume or CV
9. I did not have any goals when I applies for this workshop
10. Other (specify)

<span style="color: gray;">Finding: According to exact binomial tests performed on each category, most participants reported that they were interested in learning about models, software tools, and questions before the workshop.</span>

</div>

<div class = "col-md-6">

```{r q2preplot, message=FALSE}
# Getting response counts
responses <- rep(0,10)
# Looping over the options and counting how many participants checked the box (value = 1)
for (i in 1:10) {responses[i] <- sum(data[, (which(colnames(data) == "pre2a___1") - 1 + i)] == 1,na.rm=TRUE)}
# Getting any custom responses (there were none)
other <- data$pre2b[which(data$pre2a___10 == 1)]
# Storing response counts in a dataframe
data_q2 <- data.frame(cbind(response = 1:10, number = responses))
data_q2$response <- c("Questions", "Models", "Software", "Coding", "Decide", "Discuss", "Network", "Resume", "None", "Other")

# Plotting output
levels <- c("Models", "Questions", "Software", "Network", "Coding", "Decide", "Discuss", "Resume", "None", "Other")
plot_q2pre <- ggplot(data = data_q2, aes(x = factor(response,levels=levels), y = number)) +
  geom_col(fill = color1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = number), hjust = 1.25, color = "white", size = 6) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = rev,
                   labels = c("Other",
                              "None",
                              "Resume/CV",
                              "Discuss research",
                              "Decide future research",
                              "Try coding",
                              "Network",
                              "Learn software tools",
                              "Learn about questions",
                              "Learn models")) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size=12,color="black"),
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        panel.border = element_blank())
ggsave("./output/q2pre.png",plot_q2pre,width=6,height=3)
include_graphics("./output/q2pre.png")

# For each row (attendee), determining how many boxes were checked
start_ind <- which(colnames(data) == "pre2a___1")
row_sums <- c()
for (i in 1:nrow(data)) {
  row_sum <- sum(data[i,start_ind:(start_ind + 9)],na.rm=T)
  row_sums <- c(row_sums,row_sum)
}
# Counting the participants who checked at least one box, i.e. the sample size
num_samples <- sum(row_sums != 0)

# Exact binomial tests to determine whether more than 50% of participants expressed a goal
models_p <- binom.test(data_q2$number[2],num_samples,p=0.5,alternative="g")$p.value
software_p <- binom.test(data_q2$number[3],num_samples,p=0.5,alternative="g")$p.value
questions_p <- binom.test(data_q2$number[1],num_samples,p=0.5,alternative="g")$p.value

# Turning counts into percentages (count / sample size)
models_percent <- round(data_q2$number[which(data_q2$response == "Models")] / num_samples, 2)
software_percent <- round(data_q2$number[which(data_q2$response == "Software")] / num_samples, 2)
questions_percent <- round(data_q2$number[which(data_q2$response == "Questions")] / num_samples, 2)
decide_percent <- round(data_q2$number[which(data_q2$response == "Decide")] / num_samples, 2)

# Printing percentages and test results
cat(" N = ", num_samples, "\n",
    "Exact binomial test", "\n",
    "Models:    ", models_percent, " | p = ", models_p, "\n", 
    "Software:  ", software_percent, " | p = ", software_p, "\n", 
    "Questions: ", questions_percent, " | p = ", questions_p, "\n",
    "Decide:    ", decide_percent)
```

Question 3: Please rate your experience with the following topics and tools:

a. Probability and statistics
b. Molecular phylogenetics
c. Divergence time estimation
d. Biogeographic models
e. Bayesian models
f. Markov chain Monte Carlo
g. Unix command line
h. RevBayes

Options: Unfamiliar, somewhat familiar, competent, highly competent, expert

<span style="color: gray;">Finding: According to an exact binomial test comparing the combined "somewhat familiar" and "competent" categories with all other categories, most participants were either "somewhat familiar" or "competent" across topics (excluding RevBayes). According to an exact binomial  test comparing the combined "highly competent" and "expert" categories with all other categories, few participants rated themselves as highly competent or expert across topics (excluding RevBayes). According to the exact Wilcoxon signed rank test comparing the responses for the RevBayes topic to the second-most unfamiliar topic (biogeographic models), the most unfamiliar topic was RevBayes.</span>

</div>

<div class = "col-md-7">

```{r q3preplot, message=FALSE}
# Counting responses
questions <- c("Probability and statistics", "Molecular phylogenetics", "Divergence time estimation", "Biogeographic models", "Bayesian models", "Markov chain Monte Carlo", "Unix command line", "RevBayes")
answers <- c("Unfamiliar", "Somewhat familiar", "Competent", "Highly competent", "Expert")
data_q3_subset <- data[(which(colnames(data) == "pre3a")):(which(colnames(data) == "pre3a") + 7)]
# Creating a matrix to store response counts for each question
data_q3 <- matrix(ncol=3,nrow=8*5)
# Looping over each question and response to count the number of instances
row <- 1
for (i in 1:8) {
  for (j in 1:5) {
    data_q3[row,1] <- questions[i]
    data_q3[row,2] <- answers[j]
    data_q3[row,3] <- sum((data_q3_subset[,i]) == j, na.rm = TRUE)
    row <- row + 1
  }
}
# Turning the matrix of response counts into a dataframe
data_q3 <- data.frame(data_q3)
colnames(data_q3) <- c("question", "answer", "count")
data_q3$count <- as.numeric(data_q3$count)

# Number of responses over all topics except RevBayes
colsums <- 0
for (i in 1:7) {
  colsum <- sum(!is.na(data_q3_subset[[i]]))
  colsums <- colsums + colsum
}

# Plotting output
plot_q3pre <- ggplot(data = data_q3, aes(x = factor(question, levels = questions), y = factor(answer, levels = answers), fill = count)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = count), color = "black", size = 6) +
  scale_x_discrete(limits = rev,
                   expand = c(0,0),
                 labels = c("RevBayes",
                            "Command line",
                            "Markov chain Monte Carlo",
                            "Bayesian models",
                            "Biogeographic models",
                            "Divergence time estimation",
                            "Molecular phylogenetics",
                            "Probability and statistics")) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0,0),
                    labels = c("Unfamiliar",
                              "Somewhat\nfamiliar",
                              "Competent",
                              "Highly\ncompetent",
                              "Expert")) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low="white", high=color1) +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size=12,color="black"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size=10,color="black"),
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none")
ggsave("./output/q3pre.png",plot_q3pre,width=6,height=4)
include_graphics("./output/q3pre.png")

# Combining some response types for statistical tests, excluding RevBayes
familiar_or_competent <- data_q3$count[which(data_q3$answer[1:35]=="Somewhat familiar")] + data_q3$count[which(data_q3$answer[1:35]=="Competent")]
not_familiar_or_competent <- data_q3$count[which(data_q3$answer[1:35]=="Highly competent")] + data_q3$count[which(data_q3$answer[1:35]=="Expert")] + data_q3$count[which(data_q3$answer[1:35]=="Unfamiliar")]

# Combining some response types for statistical tests, excluding RevBayes
highly_or_expert <- data_q3$count[which(data_q3$answer[1:35]=="Highly competent")] + data_q3$count[which(data_q3$answer[1:35]=="Expert")]
not_highly_or_expert <- data_q3$count[which(data_q3$answer[1:35]=="Unfamiliar")] + data_q3$count[which(data_q3$answer[1:35]=="Somewhat familiar")] + data_q3$count[which(data_q3$answer[1:35]=="Competent")]

# Exact binomial test for somewhat familiar / competent versus other responses
somewhat_or_competent_test <- binom.test(sum(familiar_or_competent,na.rm=T),colsums,p=0.5,alternative="g")$p.value
somewhat_or_competent_percent <- round(sum(familiar_or_competent) / (sum(familiar_or_competent) + sum(not_familiar_or_competent)),2)
# Exact binomial test test for highly competent / expert versus other responses
highly_or_expert_test <- binom.test(sum(highly_or_expert,na.rm=T),colsums,p=0.5,alternative="l")$p.value
highly_or_expert_percent <- round(sum(highly_or_expert) / (sum(highly_or_expert) + sum(not_highly_or_expert)),2)
# Exact Wilcoxon signed rank test for RevBayes versus the next-least-familiar category, models
unfamiliar_test <- wilcox.exact(data$pre3d,data$pre3h,paired=T,alternative="g")$p.value
mean_rb_familiarity <- round(mean(data$pre3h,na.rm=T),2)

# For each row (attendee), determining the sum of all responses
start_ind <- which(colnames(data) == "pre3a")
row_sums <- c()
for (i in 1:nrow(data)) {
  row_sum <- sum(data[i,start_ind:(start_ind + 7)],na.rm=TRUE)
  row_sums <- c(row_sums,row_sum)
}
# Counting the participants who submitted at least one response, i.e. the sample size
N <- sum(row_sums != 0)

# Printing percentages and test results
cat(" N = ", N, "\n",
    "Exact binomial test", "\n",
    "Somewhat familiar & competent: ", somewhat_or_competent_percent, " | p = ", somewhat_or_competent_test, "\n", 
    "Highly competent & expert:      ", highly_or_expert_percent, " | p = ", highly_or_expert_test, "\n",
    "Exact Wilcoxon signed rank test", "\n",
    "Unfamiliar models vs. RevBayes:       | p = ", unfamiliar_test, "\n",
    "Mean RevBayes familiarity:     ", mean_rb_familiarity)
```

</div>

Question 4: During your time as a researcher, how often have the following events occurred?

* I wanted to use a research method, but stopped because the *software* was too difficult to use.
* I used a research method even though the *software* was difficult to use.
* I wanted to use a research method, but stopped because the *programming* was too difficult.
* I used a research method even though the *programming* was difficult.
* I wanted to use a research method, but stopped because the *statistical analysis* was too difficult.
* I used a research method even though the *statistical analysis* was difficult.
* I wanted to use a research method, but stopped because the *model* was too difficult to understand.
* I used a research method even though the *model* was difficult to understand.

Options: Never, Rarely, Sometimes, Often, Very often

<span style="color: gray;">Finding: According to exact Wilcoxon signed rank tests (both pairwise for each challenge and overall), participants indicated that they were significantly more likely to continue research despite a variety of challenges than to stop due to those challenges.</span>

</div>

<div class = "col-md-6">

```{r q4preplot, message=FALSE}
# Counting responses
questions <- c("Software -- Stopped", "Software -- Continued", "Programming -- Stopped", "Programming -- Continued", "Statistics -- Stopped", "Statistics -- Continued", "Model -- Stopped", "Model -- Continued")
answers <- c("Never", "Rarely", "Sometimes", "Often", "Very often")
data_q4_subset <- data[(which(colnames(data) == "pre4a")):(which(colnames(data) == "pre4a") + 7)]
# Creating a matrix to store response counts for each question
data_q4 <- matrix(ncol=3,nrow=8*5)
# Looping over each question and response to count the number of instances
row <- 1
for (i in 1:8) {
  for (j in 1:5) {
    data_q4[row,1] <- questions[i]
    data_q4[row,2] <- answers[j]
    data_q4[row,3] <- sum((data_q4_subset[,i]) == j, na.rm = TRUE)
    row <- row + 1
  }
}
# Turning the matrix of response counts into a dataframe
data_q4 <- data.frame(data_q4)
colnames(data_q4) <- c("question", "answer", "count")
data_q4$count <- as.numeric(data_q4$count)

# Plotting output
plot_q4pre <- ggplot(data = data_q4, aes(x = factor(question, levels = questions), y = factor(answer, levels = answers), fill = count)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = count), color = "black", size = 6) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0,0),
                   limits = rev,
                   labels = c("Continued despite the model",
                              "Stopped because of the model",
                              "Continued despite statistics",
                              "Stopped due to statistics",
                              "Continued despite programming",
                              "Stopped due to programming",
                              "Continued despite software",
                              "Stopped due to software")) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0,0)) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low="white", high=color1) +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size=10,color="black"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size=12,color="black"),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none")
ggsave("./output/q4pre.png",plot_q4pre,width=6,height=4)
include_graphics("./output/q4pre.png")

# Exact Wilcoxon signed rank tests comparing distribution of "stopped" versus "continued" for each topic and all topics combined
software_p <- wilcox.exact(data$pre4a,data$pre4b,paired=T,alternative="l")$p.value
programming_p <- wilcox.exact(data$pre4c,data$pre4d,paired=T,alternative="l")$p.value
statistics_p <- wilcox.exact(data$pre4e,data$pre4f,paired=T,alternative="l")$p.value
model_p <- wilcox.exact(data$pre4g,data$pre4h,paired=T,alternative="l")$p.value
total_p <- wilcox.exact(c(data$pre4a,data$pre4c,data$pre4e,data$pre4g),c(data$pre4b,data$pre4d,data$pre4f,data$pre4h),paired=T,alternative="l")$p.value

# Calculating mean responses
stop <- round(mean(c(data$pre4a, data$pre4c, data$pre4e, data$pre4g),na.rm=T),2)
continue <- round(mean(c(data$pre4b, data$pre4d, data$pre4f, data$pre4h),na.rm=T),2)

# For each row (attendee), determining the sum of all responses
start_ind <- which(colnames(data) == "pre4a")
row_sums <- c()
for (i in 1:nrow(data)) {
  row_sum <- sum(data[i,start_ind:(start_ind + 7)],na.rm=TRUE)
  row_sums <- c(row_sums,row_sum)
}
# Counting the participants who submitted at least one response, i.e. the sample size
N <- sum(row_sums != 0)

# Printing percentages and test results
cat(" N = ", N, "\n", 
    "Exact Wilcoxon signed rank test", "\n",
    "Software:    p = ", software_p, "\n", 
    "Programming: p = ", programming_p, "\n", 
    "Statistics:  p = ", statistics_p, "\n", 
    "Model:       p = ", model_p, "\n", 
    "Total:       p = ", total_p, "\n", 
    "Stop mean response:     ", stop, "\n",
    "Continue mean response: ", continue)
```

Question 1: Did this workshop meet your expectation? Why or why not?

Coded Responses:

* Did not meet expectations
* Partly met expectations
* Met expectations
* Exceeded expectations

<span style="color: gray;">Finding: According to the exact binomial test on the combined number of participants who indicated that their expectations were met and exceeded, participants felt that their expectations for the workshop were met or exceeded.</span>

</div>

<div class = "col-md-6">

```{r q1postplot, message=FALSE}
# Coding responses
post1code_list <- c("M",NA,"M","P","M","M","E","M","M","E",NA,NA,"P","P","M","M",NA,NA,NA,"M",NA,NA,NA,NA,NA,NA,"M",NA,NA,NA,"M",NA,"P",NA,NA,NA,NA,"E",NA,"M",NA,NA,"M",NA,NA,"M",NA,NA,"P","M","O",NA,"M",NA,NA,NA,"P",NA,NA,"M",NA,"M","M","M","M","M",NA,NA)
data_post1code <- data.frame(post1code=post1code_list)

# Plotting output (y/n)
levels1 <- c("O","N", "P", "M", "E")
plot_q1post <- ggplot(data = subset(data_post1code, !is.na(post1code)), aes(x = factor(post1code, levels = levels1))) +
  geom_bar(fill = color1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ..count..), stat = "count", hjust = 1.25, color = "white", size = 6) +
  scale_x_discrete(drop = F,
                   labels = c("Other",
                              "Did not meet expectations",
                              "Partly met expectations",
                              "Met expectations",
                              "Exceeded expectations")) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
  theme_bw() +
  coord_flip() +
  theme(axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size=12,color="black"),
        axis.text.x = element_blank(),
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        panel.border = element_blank())
ggsave("./output/q1post.png",plot_q1post,width=6,height=3)
include_graphics("./output/q1post.png")

# Countin the total number of responses
num_samples <- length(post1code_list[which(!is.na(post1code_list))])
# Combining the totals for "meets expectations" and "exceeds expectations"
met_count <- sum(data_post1code=="M",na.rm=T) + sum(data_post1code=="E",na.rm=T)
# Performing exact binomial test for "meets or exceeds" versus other categories
met_p <- binom.test(met_count,num_samples,p=0.5,alternative="g")$p.value
met_percent <- round(met_count / num_samples, 2)

# Printing test results and percentage
cat(" N = ", num_samples, "\n",
    "Exact binomial test", "\n",
    "Met & exceeded: ", met_percent, " | p = ", met_p)
```

Question 2: For each of the following topics and tools, please indicate how your level of confidence in your ability to use the tool has *changed* after engaging in the workshop.

a. Probability and statistics
b. Molecular phylogenetics
c. Divergence time estimation
d. Biogeographic models
e. Bayesian models
f. Markov chain Monte Carlo
g. Unix command line
h. RevBayes

Options: Much less confident, less confident, about the same, more confident, much more confident

<span style="color: gray;">Finding: According to exact binomial tests for each topic on the combined "more confident" and "much more confident" response categories compared to all other response categories, for RevBayes and biogeographic models (the topics with the least prior experience and the most prevalent participant goals, not statistically tested), confidence significantly improved.</span>

</div>

<div class = "col-md-6">

```{r q2postplot, message=FALSE}
# Counting responses
questions <- c("Probability and statistics", "Molecular phylogenetics", "Divergence time estimation", "Biogeographic models", "Bayesian models", "Markov chain Monte Carlo", "Unix command line", "RevBayes")
answers <- c("Much less confident", "Less confident", "About the same", "More confident", "Much more confident")
data_q2_subset <- data[(which(colnames(data) == "post2a")):(which(colnames(data) == "post2a") + 7)]
data_q2 <- matrix(ncol=3,nrow=8*5)
row <- 1
for (i in 1:8) {
  for (j in 1:5) {
    data_q2[row,1] <- questions[i]
    data_q2[row,2] <- answers[j]
    data_q2[row,3] <- sum((data_q2_subset[,i]) == j, na.rm = TRUE)
    row <- row + 1
  }
}
data_q2 <- data.frame(data_q2)
colnames(data_q2) <- c("question", "answer", "count")
data_q2$count <- as.numeric(data_q2$count)

# Plotting output
plot_q2post <- ggplot(data = data_q2, aes(x = factor(question, levels = questions), y = factor(answer, levels = answers), fill = count)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = count), color = "black", size = 6) +
    scale_x_discrete(limits = rev,
                     expand = c(0,0),
                   labels = c("RevBayes",
                              "Unix command line",
                              "Markov chain Monte Carlo",
                              "Bayesian models",
                              "Biogeographic models",
                              "Divergence time estimation",
                              "Molecular phylogenetics",
                              "Probability and statistics")) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0,0),
                   labels = c("Much less\nconfident",
                              "Less\nconfident",
                              "About\nthe same",
                              "More\nconfident",
                              "Much more\nconfident")) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low="white", high=color1) +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size=12,color="black"),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size=10,color="black"),
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none")
ggsave("./output/q2post.png",plot_q2post,width=6,height=4)
include_graphics("./output/q2post.png")

# Getting sample size
start_ind <- which(colnames(data) == "post2a")
row_sums <- c()
for (i in 1:nrow(data)) {
  row_sum <- sum(data[i,start_ind:(start_ind + 7)],na.rm=TRUE)
  row_sums <- c(row_sums,row_sum)
}
num_samples <- sum(row_sums != 0)

# Exact binomial tests for more & much more confident versus other responses for models and RevBayes
model_count <- sum(data$post2d==4,na.rm=T) + sum(data$post2d==5,na.rm=T)
model_p <- binom.test(model_count,num_samples,p=0.5,alternative="g")$p.value
model_average <- round(mean(data$post2d,na.rm=T),2)
rb_count <- sum(data$post2h==4,na.rm=T) + sum(data$post2h==5,na.rm=T)
rb_p <- binom.test(rb_count,num_samples,p=0.5,alternative="g")$p.value
rb_average <- round(mean(data$post2h,na.rm=T),2)

# Printing test results and percentages
cat(" N = ", num_samples, "\n",
    "Exact binomial test", "\n",
    "Biogeographic models: ", model_average, " | p = ", model_p, "\n",
    "RevBayes:            ", rb_average, " | p = ", rb_p, "\n")
```

<div class = "col-md-6">

<span style="color: gray;">For individuals who completed both the pre-workshop survey and the post-workshop survey, we also compared confidence improvement to initial experience level. Across topics, it appears that individuals with less experience had greater confidence improvements (no statistical tests performed).</span>

</div>

<div class = "col-md-6">

```{r prepost, message=FALSE}
# Getting pre-workshop experience and post-workshop confidence for each topic
start_ind <- which(colnames(data)=="pre3a")
data_preconf <- unlist(data[start_ind:(start_ind+7)],use.names=F)
start_ind <- which(colnames(data)=="post2a")
data_postconf <- unlist(data[start_ind:(start_ind+7)],use.names=F)
data_conf <- data.frame(cbind(pre=data_preconf,post=data_postconf))
conf_matrix <- matrix(0,nrow=5,ncol=5)

# Generating matrix of pairwise counts for pre- and post-workshop responses
for (ind in 1:length(data_preconf)) {
  i <- data_preconf[ind]
  j <- data_postconf[ind]
  if (!is.na(i) & !is.na(j)) {
    conf_matrix[i,j] <- conf_matrix[i,j] + 1
  }
}

conf_props <- conf_matrix

# Turning counts into per-row proportions
for (i in 1:5) {
  for (j in 1:5) {
    conf_props[i,j] <- round(conf_matrix[i,j] / sum(conf_matrix[i,]),2)
    if (is.na(conf_props[i,j])) {conf_props[i,j] <- 0}
  }
}

i_vals <- c()
j_vals <- c()
props <- c()

# Turning count proportions into "long" data
for (i in 1:5) {
  for (j in 1:5) {
    i_vals <- c(i_vals,i)
    j_vals <- c(j_vals, j)
    props <- c(props, conf_props[i,j])
  }
}

conf_props <- cbind(pre=i_vals, post=j_vals, prop=props)

# Plotting pre-workshop experience versus post-workshop confidence
plot_conf <- ggplot(data = conf_props, aes(x = factor(pre), y = factor(post), fill = prop)) +
  geom_tile() +
  geom_text(aes(label = prop), color = "black", size = 6) +
  scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0,0),
                   labels = c("Unfamiliar",
                              "Somewhat familiar",
                              "Competent",
                              "Highly competent",
                              "Expert")) +
  scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0,0),
                   labels = c("Much less\nconfident",
                              "Less\nconfident",
                              "About\nthe same",
                              "More\nconfident",
                              "Much more\nconfident")) +
  scale_fill_gradient(low="white", high=color1) +
  coord_flip() +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size=10,color="black"),
        axis.text.y = element_text(size=12,color="black"),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none",
        aspect.ratio = 1)
ggsave("./output/conf.png",plot_conf,width=6,height=5)
include_graphics("./output/conf.png")
```

```{r q7postplot, message=FALSE}
        axis.text.y = element_text(size=12,color="black"),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        legend.position = "none")
ggsave("./output/q7post.png",plot_q7post,width=6,height=3)
include_graphics("./output/q7post.png")

lecture <- data$post7a
plc <- data$post7d

# Adding non-lecture results, but dividing by 4 to ensure same sample size as lecture results
other <- (data$post7b + data$post7c + data$post7d + data$post7e) / 4
# Exact Wilcoxon rank-sign test to compare lectures to non-lectures
lecture_p <- wilcox.exact(lecture,other,paired=T,alternative="g")$p.value
lecture_mean <- round(mean(lecture,na.rm=T),2)
other_mean <- round(mean(other,na.rm=T),2)

# Exact binomial test comparing helpful & very helpful to other categories for participatory live coding
plc_mean <- round(mean(plc,na.rm=T),2)
num_samples <- sum(!is.na(data$post7d))
plc_count <- sum(data$post7d==5,na.rm=T) + sum(data$post7d==4,na.rm=T)
plc_percent <- round(plc_count / num_samples,2)
plc_p <- binom.test(plc_count,num_samples,p=0.5,alternative="g")$p.value

# Getting sample size
start_ind <- which(colnames(data) == "post7a")
row_sums <- c()
for (i in 1:nrow(data)) {
  row_sum <- sum(data[i,start_ind:(start_ind + 4)],na.rm=TRUE)
  row_sums <- c(row_sums,row_sum)
}
N <- sum(row_sums != 0)

# Printing statistical test results and percentages
cat(" N = ", N, "\n",
    "Exact Wilcoxon signed rank test", "\n",
    "Lecture vs. other:                  p = ", lecture_p, "\n",
    "Exact binomial test", "\n",
    "PLC:                       ", plc_percent, " | p = ", plc_p, "\n",
    "Lecture mean response:     ", lecture_mean, "\n",
    "Non-lecture mean response: ", other_mean, "\n",
    "PLC mean response:         ", plc_mean)
```

Question 9: Do you think the *participatory live coding* activity will make it easier to implement phylogenetic models of historical biogeography in the future?

Options: Much less easy, less easy, about the same, more easy, much more easy, I did not participate in this activity

<span style="color: gray;">Finding: According to the exact binomial test comparing the combined "more easy" and "much more easy" categories to all other categories, participants did not indicate that participatory live coding would make it easier to implement the models in the future.</span>

```{r q9postplot, message=FALSE}
# Replacing numerical responses with strings
mean_response <- round(mean(data$post9,na.rm=T),2)
data$post9 <- gsub(1, "Much less easy", data$post9)
data$post9 <- gsub(2, "Less easy", data$post9)
data$post9 <- gsub(3, "About the same", data$post9)
data$post9 <- gsub(4, "More easy", data$post9)
data$post9 <- gsub(5, "Much more easy", data$post9)
data$post9 <- gsub(6, "Did not participate", data$post9)

# Plotting output
levels <- c("Much less easy", "Less easy", "About the same", "More easy", "Much more easy", "Did not participate")
plot_q9post <- ggplot(data = subset(data, !is.na(post9)), aes(x = factor(post9, levels = levels))) +
  geom_bar(fill = color1) +
  geom_text(aes(label = ..count..), stat = "count", vjust = 1.25, color = "white", size = 6) +
  scale_x_discrete(drop = F,
                   labels = c("Much\nless easy",
                              "Less easy",
                              "About\nthe same",
                              "More easy",
                              "Much\nmore easy",
                              "Did not\nparticipate")) +
  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0)) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.ticks.y = element_blank(),
        axis.ticks.x = element_blank(),
        axis.text.y = element_blank(),
        axis.text.x = element_text(size=12,color="black"),
        axis.title.y = element_blank(),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank(),
        panel.border = element_blank())
ggsave("./output/q9post.png",plot_q9post,width=6,height=5)
include_graphics("./output/q9post.png")

# Exact binomial test comparing more & much more easy to other responses
num_samples <- sum(!is.na(data$post9))
more_count <- sum(data$post9=="More easy",na.rm=T) + sum(data$post9=="Much more easy",na.rm=T)
more_p <- binom.test(more_count,num_samples,p=0.5,alternative="g")$p.value
more_percent <- round(more_count / num_samples, 2)

# Printing statistical test results and percentages
cat(" N = ", num_samples, "\n",
    "Exact binomial test", "\n",
    "More & much more easy: ", more_percent, " | p = ", more_p, "\n",
    "Mean response:         ", mean_response)
```
